name: cli completions
statement: The completions command writes a shell completion script to standard output. It accepts every shell that the completion library defines, which includes bash, zsh, and fish.

name: config contract version gate
statement: The system accepts a provider contract version only when that version is in the supported set. The supported set holds the current version and the version before it. The error names the supported versions. The system checks the version only for a provider that comes from a configuration file.

name: config env override vars
statement: The system reads provider command overrides from NOSCOPE_MINT_CMD, NOSCOPE_REFRESH_CMD, and NOSCOPE_REVOKE_CMD. The system treats an empty variable as unset.

name: config name allowlist
statement: The system accepts a provider or profile name only when every character is an ASCII letter, digit, hyphen, underscore, or dot. The system rejects the empty name. The system rejects the names dot and double dot.

name: config not found lists locations
statement: When no configuration layer supplies a provider, the system reports the provider as not found. The error lists three fixed candidate locations. Those locations are a command-line flag, an environment variable, and a configuration file path.

name: config precedence no merge
statement: Provider commands come from exactly one configuration layer. Direct overrides beat environment variables. Environment variables beat the configuration file. The system never merges values from two layers. A winning override layer can leave the mint command empty without an error.

name: config provider toml schema
statement: A provider configuration file must declare contract_version and a commands table with a non-empty mint command. The system rejects a provider file that lacks either of those fields. The system ignores keys it does not recognise.

name: cross capability consistency
statement: A provider that declares support for refresh or revoke must also configure the matching command. The system rejects an inconsistent provider configuration when it parses the configuration file.

name: cross command parse quoting
statement: The system splits a configured command string into arguments with POSIX shell quoting rules and keeps a quoted segment as one argument. On unbalanced quoting it falls back to whitespace splitting.

name: cross config file permissions
statement: The system refuses to read a provider or profile configuration file that is group-writable or grants any permission to other users. The same check covers both file kinds. The check runs before the system reads the file content.

name: cross revoke idempotent exit0
statement: A revoke command that exits with status 0 counts as success. The provider script decides whether an already revoked credential exits 0. No production code inspects revoke stderr for already revoked or expired text.

name: cross rollback budget
statement: The run rollback revokes each token under a separate 5 second wall clock budget and at most 3 retries. Delays start at 100 milliseconds and double. The rollback handles tokens one after another, so the total rollback time grows with the token count. A zero budget skips revocation, but no production caller passes zero.

name: cross single conversion path
statement: Provider output becomes an in-memory credential through one conversion function. The function attaches the role, the provider name and a credential identifier that the caller supplies, and it keeps the expiry that the parser produced.

name: cross template substitution
statement: The system replaces {role} and {ttl} in every argument of a provider mint command before it runs that command. The system performs no substitution on a revoke command. An unknown placeholder such as {unknown} stays in the argument unchanged.

name: cross terminal refusal
statement: The mint command refuses to write credentials when stdout is a terminal. It exits with code 64. The --force-terminal flag overrides the refusal.

name: doctor checks
statement: The doctor command first checks that the noscope config directory exists. When that directory exists, doctor checks each TOML file directly inside the providers subdirectory. Doctor also checks each mint, refresh, and revoke command that such a file configures. Doctor stops after the first check when the config directory is missing.

name: doctor exit codes
statement: The doctor exit code shows the worst check status. All passing gives 0, warnings only give 1, and any failure gives 78.

name: errors json error object
statement: When a command returns an error and the operator selected JSON output, main writes one JSON object to standard error. The object carries the status, the command name, the error kind, and the message. In text mode main writes one line that starts with noscope and a colon.

name: errors six kinds
statement: Every failure that the Error type carries names one category from a closed set of six. The categories are usage, config, provider, security, profile, and internal.

name: events log format strict
statement: The log format parser accepts only the lowercase words json and text. It rejects every other value, including any other capitalization.

name: events single line
statement: The system writes every JSON event as one compact line. EventEmitter::format_event produces every line that the system emits. A text event may break across lines when the error message contains a line break.

name: exec exit0 only mints
statement: The system accepts a minted credential only when the provider command exits with code 0. Output that looks valid but arrives with a non-zero exit produces a mint failure instead of a credential.

name: exec exit interpretation
statement: The system treats a provider exit code outside 0 to 4 as a general error. When the raw code is above 128 the system also records the signal number as the code minus 128. A raw code of exactly 128 records no signal number. A process that a signal really killed reports no code, so the system substitutes 1 and records no signal number.

name: exec expiry fallback
statement: When a provider omits the expiry, the system sets the expiry to the current time plus the requested time to live. The system records that the provider did not supply the expiry.

name: exec output token contract
statement: A provider mint command must print a JSON object with a token field that holds a non-empty string. The system rejects output that has no such token field. When the output carries an expires_at field, that field must be a valid ISO 8601 timestamp. The system accepts an expires_at timestamp that lies in the past, to tolerate provider clock skew. When expires_at is absent or null, the system computes the expiry from the requested TTL.

name: exec stderr redaction
statement: The system replaces the value of every variable whose name starts with NOSCOPE_TOKEN with the text [redacted] in captured provider standard error. No live command passes a credential value in such a variable, so this replacement removes nothing today. The system never redacts the credential that the provider itself printed. The system truncates standard error before it redacts, so a value that straddles the cut can leave a prefix behind.

name: exec stderr truncate
statement: The system keeps at most 4096 bytes of provider standard error. The cut never splits a UTF-8 character.

name: exec stdout 1mib cap
statement: The system rejects provider standard output that is larger than 1 mebibyte and mints no credential from it. Output of exactly 1 mebibyte is accepted. The system reads the whole output into memory before it applies this check, so the check does not bound memory use.

name: Child exit code passthrough
statement: Noscope maps a child exit status to one integer. A normal exit gives the exact child exit code. A signal death gives 128 plus the signal number. Any other status gives 1.

name: Expiry warns and never stops the child
statement: The expiry of one credential never stops the child process. The expiry never triggers a new mint. Noscope warns the operator and names the provider and the token identifier.

name: init creates 0700
statement: The init command creates the noscope directory and its providers and profiles subdirectories under the config home. It sets mode 0700 on each of those three directories after it creates that directory. It does not set the mode on any parent directory it creates. It does not tighten a directory that already exists.

name: init idempotent
statement: A second run of the init command does not fail. It skips every path that is already a directory, so it does not change the permissions of an existing directory.

name: orchestration bounded concurrency
statement: The orchestrator holds a semaphore permit for each provider mint attempt, so concurrent attempts never exceed the configured limit. The run and mint commands set that limit to 8.

name: orchestration per provider timeout
statement: The orchestrator applies its own timeout to each provider mint attempt. The run and mint commands set that timeout to 30 seconds. A provider that exceeds the timeout becomes a failed provider.

name: orchestration timeout error names provider
statement: A provider timeout error names the provider and the configured timeout in whole seconds. The message does not report the measured elapsed time.

name: profile named must exist
statement: A profile that the operator names must exist. The system reports an error that includes the path when the named profile file is missing.

name: profile schema
statement: A profile must list at least one credential. Each credential must give a non-empty provider name. Each credential must give a non-empty role. Each credential must give a whole-number TTL greater than zero.

name: Refresh only when due and child alive
statement: Noscope runs a refresh command only for credentials whose refresh time has arrived. Noscope runs no refresh command after the child process exits.

name: refresh never disabled for good
statement: A run of failed refreshes never disables refresh for good. The credential returns to its normal refresh time after the failure window. The next attempt always waits at least 1 second.

name: Refresh failure never kills child
statement: A failed credential refresh never stops the child process. Noscope retries the refresh with growing delays. After the retries run out, noscope lets the credential expire.

name: Refresh failure isolation
statement: Noscope tracks refresh failures separately for each credential. A failure on one credential never changes the retry state of another credential.

name: refresh retry params
statement: Refresh retries start at 1 second and double on each attempt. Noscope stops after 4 retries. Each retry delay varies by up to 25 percent. Noscope skips a retry whose delay exceeds half of the credential lifetime that remains.

name: Point-in-time injection warning
statement: Noscope warns at startup whenever refresh is active. The warning states that noscope injects environment variables once at spawn time. The warning states that the running child never sees a refreshed credential.

name: Per-credential refresh at 75 percent
statement: Noscope computes a refresh time for each credential from that credential's own expiry. The refresh time falls at 75 percent of the granted lifetime. Noscope never merges credentials into one shared schedule.

name: Identifier-only revoke
statement: Noscope revokes a credential with the credential identifier and the provider name alone. A revoke command never receives the credential value.

name: Role character set on every input path
statement: Noscope rejects a role that holds any character outside ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, and dots. The check applies to command flags and to profile credentials.

name: signals event honesty
statement: The system emits a signal_received event for every shutdown signal it handles. The system emits a signal_forwarded event only after a forward succeeds.

name: signals forward set
statement: The system forwards SIGTERM, SIGINT, and SIGHUP to the child process group. The system ignores every other signal the operating system delivers.

name: signals forward to group
statement: The system forwards a run mode signal to the process group whose identifier equals the child process identifier. The system signals the child alone when that group does not exist. The system treats a missing target as a completed forward.

name: signals noscope env stripped
statement: The system removes every environment variable whose name starts with NOSCOPE_ from the agent child environment. The system refuses to start the agent child when an injected key uses that prefix.

name: signals parallel revocation isolation
statement: The run command revokes every active credential in parallel when the child exits or a shutdown signal arrives. A failure for one credential does not stop the others. A panicking task yields no result, so the report can be shorter than the credential list.

name: signals process group setup
statement: On Linux the system places every run mode child in a new process group that the child leads. On Linux the kernel also sends SIGTERM to that child when noscope dies first. Other platforms apply neither protection. Mint mode applies neither protection.

name: signals signal revocation budget
statement: Signal revocation gives each credential a 10 second wall clock budget and at most 3 retries. Waits start at 500 milliseconds and double. The code checks the budget only between attempts, so one slow attempt can run past the budget.

name: token mandatory expiry
statement: A ScopedToken always carries an expiry time. Both constructors take a non-optional DateTime, so the program cannot build a credential object without an expiry.

name: token mint envelope five fields
statement: Every envelope in the mint stdout JSON array carries exactly five fields. The fields are token, expires_at, token_id, provider, and role. The expires_at field uses RFC 3339 form.

name: token redacted form no raw
statement: A RedactedToken stores only a display string that the constructor computes once. It never stores the whole credential. For a long credential the stored string still contains the first eight characters.

name: token redaction format
statement: The system hides all characters of a JWT credential and of any credential of sixteen bytes or fewer. It shows an identifier instead. For every other credential the system always shows the first eight characters followed by three dots.

name: token revoke stdin envelope
statement: The revoke command reads one JSON object from stdin. It keeps only the token_id field and the provider field. It discards the raw credential value. It rejects an object that lacks either kept field.

name: TTL bounds on every input path
statement: Noscope rejects a missing TTL. Noscope rejects a TTL below 60 seconds or above 43200 seconds. The bounds apply to command flags and to profile credentials.

name: validate checks without running
statement: The validate command checks the mint, refresh, and revoke commands of one resolved provider. It treats each whole command string as a filesystem path. It reports every command that is not an existing executable file. It collects all problems together and names the command type and the string. It runs none of those commands.
